Real captures (blectl.py stream/monitor, quiet-rest + fist-clench provocation) confirmed the complaint: GsrTracker's old auto-range normalized drive against its own recent MEAN (30s EMA), which by construction settles arousal near 1/RANGE_GAIN=0.4 at ANY steady drive level -- it can only see change relative to recent activity, never absolute arousal, so resting bounced 0.2-0.5 continuously and a deliberate clench barely stood out. Reworked GsrTracker (dsp.h + tools/dsp_v2_sim.py mirror) to normalize against a floor-TRACKER instead of a mean-tracker: fast-down/slow-up envelope (FLOOR_ATTACK_TAU=2s, FLOOR_RELEASE_TAU=180s) that tracks the quiet baseline without a sustained real SCR dragging its own normalizer up and eroding itself.
